questions.which_op_makes_the_peak: _write_merged_parquet (nested branch): pq.read_table(all partitions) + pa.concat_tables + table.take(order) + pq.write_table, executed WHILE the pandas copy of the same partition is still alive. Step peak 7.449 GiB (from 2.868 GiB before the step).
questions.all_rows_all_columns_read: yes, twice: once by pd.read_parquet (all 202 columns, all rows) and once by pq.read_table (all columns, all rows).
questions.nested_materialized_to_pandas_or_python: yes: pd.read_parquet turns every non-null struct into a Python dict holding numpy arrays (9 x 13,470 dicts); frame_content_identity then repr()s every one (408 s CPU).
questions.live_tables_batches_buffers: at the peak: pandas candidates frame (2.84 GiB RSS incl. 1.79 GiB Arrow pool kept by zero-copy numpy views) + the read_table result (2.04 GB Arrow) + the take() copy (2.01 GB Arrow) + writer buffers; after the write 6.96 GiB stays resident (allocator retention) until the frames are freed.
questions.growth: linear in total rows (every term is whole-partition); independent of row-group count; proportional to profile width (bins per profile: 2.04 GB Arrow / 13,501 rows = 151 KB/row); linear in partition count (pd.concat + concat_tables of all years). Projected full year (~24x pilot rows): ~170 GiB.

pyarrow 25 ParquetFile.iter_batches over a nested column keeps Arrow buffers alive across the WHOLE iteration (one profile column, 30-row batches: +0.05 GiB live Arrow per 600 batches, linear). This made BOTH the merge identity and the existing canonical recompute_logical_content_sha256 grow with rows: 1.90 GiB at 13,501 rows -> 3.10 GiB at 108,008 (end-to-end merge body 2.12 -> 3.10 GiB)
found_during_validation.fix: one batch reader per row group (iter_batches(row_groups=[gi])): flat (0.00-0.01 GiB live), still streams inside a large row group; hashes unchanged
